name: Secrets Management Common Pitfalls
description: This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday secrets management work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical secrets management tasks.
content:
This module lists frequently observed mistakes, bugs, and anti-patterns seen in everyday secrets management work, so they can be recognized and avoided during typical secrets management tasks.

CORE GUIDELINES
1. Before starting secrets management work, confirm the scope and constraints so the approach matches the actual requirement.
2. Document any non-obvious secrets management decision with a short rationale so future readers understand the 'why', not just the 'what'.
3. When multiple secrets management strategies are viable, name the trade-off explicitly rather than silently picking one.
4. Measure before optimizing any secrets management bottleneck; do not guess at what is slow.
5. Keep secrets management changes scoped to what was asked; avoid unrelated cleanup in the same pass.
6. Keep secrets management outputs reproducible: fix seeds, record versions, and avoid hidden non-determinism where it matters.
7. State assumptions about secrets management explicitly before proceeding, rather than leaving them implicit.
8. When secrets management guidance conflicts with a specific user instruction, defer to the user's explicit instruction and note the conflict.
9. Check that secrets management terminology is used consistently throughout, matching existing conventions in the surrounding context.
10. Validate secrets management outputs against a concrete example before treating the work as complete.
11. Surface known limitations of a chosen secrets management approach instead of presenting it as complete when it is not.
12. Prefer the simplest secrets management approach that satisfies the requirement over a more general one that isn't needed yet.

COMMON PITFALLS TO AVOID
- Avoid mixing unrelated secrets management concerns into a single change; keep each change focused.
- Do not apply generic secrets management advice without checking it fits the specific context at hand.
- Do not treat a single passing example as full verification of secrets management correctness.

CLOSING NOTE
Revisit these secrets management guidelines if the task's constraints change significantly during the work.
